mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen in each of the last four weekly means (4.7 to 7.1 percent above baseline), evidence that commuting routines are being restored. The resulting weekday footfall in office districts lifts retail-and-recreation trips, so the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC exceeds the trailing 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES weekly mean rose from 4.7 to 7.1 across t-3w to t-0w
regime_hint: gradual reopening under no new restrictions
failure_condition: The 28-day forward mean of RETAIL_REC is at or below its trailing 28-day mean despite WORKPLACES posting four consecutive weekly increases above baseline.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has crossed above +2.0 percent above baseline for the first time in the window (2.1 at t-0w). Once transit ridership clears that level, non-commute trips to malls and eateries follow with a short lag, so RETAIL_REC rises above its trailing mean within two weeks of the crossing.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean crosses above +2.0 percent above baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT weekly mean moved from 0.9 to 2.1 over the four-week window
regime_hint: steady state with mild transit normalization
failure_condition: In the two weeks after TRANSIT closes above +2.0 percent, the RETAIL_REC weekly mean does not exceed its trailing 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The joint recovery of PARKS from -7.6 to -2.6 and TRANSIT above baseline (2.1) shows households resuming discretionary out-of-home trips. Neither series alone is sufficient: it is the simultaneous restoration of outdoor leisure and transit access that lifts retail-and-recreation footfall over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS above -3.0 and TRANSIT above +1.5 in the same weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -7.6 to -2.6 while TRANSIT rose to 2.1
regime_hint: reopening with restored outdoor leisure options
failure_condition: In weeks where PARKS is above -3.0 and TRANSIT is above +1.5, the following two-week RETAIL_REC mean is not higher than the trailing 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Conditional on no new gathering restrictions, RESIDENTIAL holding flat near +3.4 while WORKPLACES climbs to +7.1 means home time is not increasing. With no residential rebound absorbing household time, discretionary retail trips expand and RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean stays below +4.0 while WORKPLACES is above +5.0
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL has stayed in a 3.4-3.9 band across all four weeks
regime_hint: no new mobility or gathering restrictions announced at or before 2021-12-15
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL jumps above +4.0 while WORKPLACES stalls below +5.0 and the 28-day forward RETAIL_REC mean stays at or below the trailing mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery-and-pharmacy mobility is unwinding from its 49.3 peak to 48.3, the first material step down in the window. As pantry stockpiling stops absorbing household budget, spending rotates into discretionary categories within about a week, so RETAIL_REC rises over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean falls at least 1.0 point below its prior-week value
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM eased from 49.3 at t-1w to 48.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: A week in which GROCERY_PHARM drops at least 1.0 point is not followed by a RETAIL_REC weekly mean above its trailing 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The decision point sits inside the late-December holiday shopping window, when gift and festive spend structurally raises retail-and-recreation footfall relative to the preceding four weeks. This calendar effect operates independently of the mobility regime and lifts RETAIL_REC over the next one to two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:decision time point 2021-12-15 falls within the December holiday shopping period
regime_hint: holiday shopping season, any restriction regime
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC weekly means across the December holiday weeks do not exceed the trailing 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery-and-pharmacy mobility stuck near +48 percent above baseline shows precautionary stockpiling has not normalized, and RESIDENTIAL remains sticky at +3.4.
